step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage CMOS operational amplifier (cascaded common-source stages with current-source loads, self-biasing feedback, and Miller compensation)
step1_figure.description: Figure 21.21 shows a common-source amplifier with a PMOS current-source load biased by the wide-swing bias circuit of Fig. 20.43 (implemented as SUB_1), with a large feedback resistor for gate-drain self-biasing and an AC input coupling capacitor. The provided netlist extends this topology into a two-stage amplifier by cascading two such common-source stages (xma/xmc and xmb/xmd) with RC Miller frequency compensation (Cc1 and Rz).

voltage_gain.description: Low-frequency small-signal open-loop voltage gain of the amplifier

equation.explanation: Each stage is a common-source amplifier with an active current-source load having gain -gm*(ro_n || ro_p). Cascading two stages yields the product of their individual stage gains.
equation.assumptions: Both NMOS and PMOS transistors in both stages are biased in the active/saturation region.

sky130_expected.calculation: With I_bias ≈ 20 uA: gm_n = sqrt(2 * 270u * (10/1) * 20u) ≈ 328 uA/V. ro_n = 1/(0.1 * 20u) = 500 kOhm, ro_p = 1/(0.1 * 20u) = 500 kOhm. Total output resistance per stage r_out = ro_n || ro_p = 250 kOhm. Single-stage gain Av1 ≈ 328 uA/V * 250 kOhm ≈ 82 V/V (38.3 dB). Two-stage gain Av = Av1 * Av2 ≈ 82 * 82 ≈ 6724 V/V ≈ 76.5 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard Sky130 1.8V transistors at ~20 uA bias typically deliver 30 to 40 dB per stage, giving 60 to 80 dB total open-loop gain.

slew_rate.description: Maximum rate of change of output voltage when charging/discharging the compensation capacitor

equation.explanation: Under large-signal slewing, the maximum available current from the first stage current source (I_bias) charges the compensation capacitor Cc1.
equation.assumptions: First stage completely steers its bias current into the compensation capacitor.

sky130_expected.calculation: SR = I_bias / Cc1 = 20 uA / 1.0 pF = 20 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Nominal bias current from the bias block is ~20 uA, and Cc1 is 1 pF, matching Ex. 21.5 directly.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Frequency at which the amplifier open-loop voltage gain drops to 0 dB (unity gain)

equation.explanation: Due to Miller pole splitting, dominant pole occurs at stage 1 output and the gain-bandwidth product is set by input transconductance divided by Miller capacitance Cc1.
equation.assumptions: Non-dominant poles are located well beyond unity gain frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: fun ≈ gma / (2*pi*Cc1) = 328 uA/V / (2 * pi * 1.0 pF) ≈ 52.2 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Transconductance of ~300 uS with 1 pF compensation capacitor gives unity-gain frequency in the 30-60 MHz range.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin of the loop gain at the unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Phase margin evaluates stability by measuring the phase difference from -180 degrees at unity gain frequency.
equation.assumptions: System is stable with dominant single-pole rolloff.

sky130_expected.calculation: Dominant pole causes 90 deg phase lag; Rz = 6.5 kOhm moves RHP zero into LHP (nulling zero near 1/(Cc*(Rz - 1/gmb))), providing lead compensation, yielding phase margin around 60 to 75 degrees.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard Miller compensation with nulling resistor Rz = 6.5 kOhm is sized to provide ~60-70 degrees of phase margin.

bias_current.description: DC bias current delivered by the current source loads

equation.explanation: The current established by the bias subcircuit SUB_1 through PMOS current mirror loads (xmc and xmd).
equation.assumptions: Bias circuit is operating at its stable operating point.

sky130_expected.calculation: The reference bias circuit from Fig. 20.43 is configured with R1 = 6.5 kOhm, targeting I_bias ≈ 20 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Table 9.1 specifies 20 uA nominal bias current for this reference generator.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent DC power consumed by the amplifier and its bias generator

equation.explanation: Total power delivered by the 1.8V supply rail to the bias network and the two amplifier branches.

sky130_expected.calculation: Amplifier branches draw 2 * 20 uA = 40 uA. Bias circuit SUB_1 has ~6 branches drawing ~120 uA. Total supply current ≈ 160 uA. P_DC = 1.8 V * 160 uA ≈ 288 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sum of currents in bias subcircuit branches plus two gain stages at VDD = 1.8V.

output_resistance.description: Small-signal AC output resistance at the amplifier output node

equation.explanation: The output resistance of the second common-source stage loaded by PMOS current source xmd.
equation.assumptions: Output node is a high-impedance drain node with both devices in saturation.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Channel-length modulation lambda ≈ 0.1 V^-1 at 20 uA gives 250 kOhm output impedance.

step3_testbench.description: ngspice testbench measuring DC operating point, power dissipation, AC small-signal open-loop gain, unity-gain bandwidth, phase margin, and transient slew rate on the two-stage amplifier netlist.
